body:
## Summary

The paired-Mac connection state is inconsistent across iOS screens when the Mac becomes unreachable.

During physical-iPhone smoke testing, turning Tailscale off on the paired Mac produced these simultaneous states:

- Settings continued to show **Connected**.
- Agents showed a yellow status and spun on “Connect securely to your paired Mac…”.
- Session loading also spun indefinitely.
- After a delay, the main Agents screen changed to **Mac offline**, but Settings still did not update.
- Turning Tailscale back on caused the app to reconnect automatically.

This makes Settings an unreliable source of truth and leaves multiple surfaces in unbounded loading states.

## Reproduction

1. Pair the signed iOS app with a Mac and confirm Agents can load.
2. Open iOS Settings and note the paired Mac shows Connected.
3. Turn Tailscale off on the paired Mac.
4. Observe Settings, Agents, and session loading for several minutes.
5. Turn Tailscale back on.

## Expected

- All screens derive connection status from one authoritative paired-host state.
- Loss of reachability changes Settings and Agents to Offline/Unavailable within a bounded timeout.
- Session loading exits to a clear offline state instead of spinning indefinitely.
- Paired-Mac mutations are disabled while offline.
- Reconnection returns every screen to Connected and performs one authoritative refresh without duplicate transcript or Activity items.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Settings and Agents show the same paired-Mac state throughout disconnect and reconnect.
- [ ] Reachability loss resolves to an explicit offline state within a documented bounded timeout.
- [ ] No paired-Mac screen can remain in an infinite loading state while the Mac is offline.
- [ ] Offline copy distinguishes “paired but unreachable” from “not paired” and “Tailscale unavailable.”
- [ ] Reconnect succeeds automatically and refreshes authoritative state once.
- [ ] Automated tests cover disconnect, stale Settings state, bounded timeout, and reconnect.
- [ ] Physical-iPhone smoke repeats the Tailscale-off/on scenario successfully.

## Context

- Found during the #1199 physical-device release smoke for PR #1165.
- Parent capability: #1171 / #1172.
- Do not include private hostnames, device identifiers, pairing codes, or tokens in test evidence.
title: iOS: keep paired-Mac connection status authoritative across Settings and Agents
